qt: to the Commission Anthony Smith (The Left) Subject:

On 31 August 2026, the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights warned that pluralism could be at risk in the elections to be held on 29 November, following the suspension of Revolución Ciudadana and then the AMIGO movement. Human Rights Watch has also documented moves to undermine the independence of judges and place restrictions on civil society. Despite these warnings, on 11 September 2026, the Commission proposed the signing and conclusion of a new Sustainable Investment Facilitation Agreement with Ecuador. On 22 October 2026, Luisa González, President Daniel Noboa’s main political opponent, was arrested and remanded in custody, in a case condemned by her movement as politically motivated. Given that Article 1 of the existing trade agreement enshrines respect for democratic principles as an essential element: 1.
What specific steps has the Commission taken to secure guarantees on electoral pluralism, judicial independence and Luisa González’s rights?

What is its justification for continuing to press forward with its proposals on the new investment agreement? Will it ask the Council to delay signing the agreement until it obtains the above guarantees?
